analysis: The only changed hunk in SSDPrefixCache.swift is retireIndexedEntries (head lines 1793-1803). Previously one removalLock critical section removed all URLs. Now SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) calls the closure per slice, and each slice takes removalLock and re-checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot. When that guard returns nil, the helper's handling is not visible here. The old code returned an empty Result in that case. If the helper aggregates nil as an empty or no-op result, the safety behavior is preserved. Slicing shortens lock hold time, which helps availability, e.g. avoiding reader or writer starvation during large TTL or LRU sweeps. This is relevant to T-041 mitigations: TTL/LRU sweeps, 30-minute sliding TTL, budget enforcement, and unlinking only through the root-safe, epoch-aware path. Between slices the lock is released, so concurrent donations or reads can interleave. SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove still validates each URL under the root and updates the index, and the stage and donate paths already tolerate absent files (forgetMissing, isAbsentBlockFailure). Epoch-store ownership is rechecked per slice, which is stricter than before. I found no new disclosure path, no change to HMAC tag derivation, DBK3 crypto, or salt scoping, and no change to the SEC-035 posture. The remaining head lines (donate, stage, readWindowSidecars, etc.) are unchanged context. I reviewed them for T-041 properties: HMAC-keyed tags, salt folding, bounded reads, weightHash/layoutEpoch bindings, and fail-closed corrupt-file removal. I saw no regression. Unverified: the removeInSlices implementation (slice size, how a nil slice result and the externalChange flag aggregate, early-stop semantics). It is outside the supplied evidence. An integration pass with that file should confirm that a mid-run ownership loss stops further slices, and that retired.removed and indexedBytesFreed stay accurate for evictOldestEntry.
